experiments.scope: The exact blake3-r2-prefix-v1 target, root instance of the construction (counter 0, flags 11; proof.md 6.4). One trial of proof.md Section 6.1 per organizer seed, each returning a 55-byte message and a 63-byte message that ends in eight zero bytes: the seven words of a context and the number of a member of the sub-class of Lemma Q2 are taken from the seed, and the pair is built by steps O, M, Y, T, S2 and S3 of Section 4. Every trial is returned. No BLAKE3 library is imported, and the returned pairs are built from the assignments of the quarter-round G and their inverses alone. The same file contains its own 2-round compression (compress2), called only by the self-test, never for a returned pair. SHAKE-256 from the standard library expands the organizer's seed into the trial's parameters. The organizer recomputes both digests. The claim of the package is for the counter instance (proof.md Sections 7 to 11), which no digest experiment can show (6.4); this experiment checks the shared construction only.
experiments.hypothesis: For every trial the two complete 2-round digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, that is on the 128 masked bits, as Lemma T of proof.md Section 6.1 states for every context and every member of the class. This is an exact claim checked on concrete inputs; it is not a test of any heuristic and not evidence of a rate or of attack cost.

experiments.scope: The exact blake3-r2-prefix-v1 target, root instance (counter 0, flags 11). The search of proof.md Section 6 at toy scale: per organizer seed one context, then the members of the sub-class in order from a member number taken from the seed, at most all 131,072 of them, stopping at the first trial whose residual has a zero low byte in digest word 1. Failed trials are returned as null pairs. The number of members tried is returned as the only observation (tries). The counter instance, its filter and its solver are not run; the program's self-test (python3 experiments/halfsearch.py --selftest N [seed], proof.md 9.3) checks them, and the organizer does not run it.
experiments.hypothesis: Every returned pair agrees on 136 digest bits: the 128 bits of the half-collision and the low byte of digest word 1. The experiment checks the trial generator and the residual computation on real digests. The members are tried in order and are not independent trials, so the number of tries is not a measurement of a rate; it is not a test of heuristic H1' or H2'' and not evidence of attack cost.

experiments.scope: The mean of the pass units X of one outer step of the counter search (proof.md 9.2 and 9.4) under the model M_X: Y4 uniform in the class of eta, Y9 and w8 uniform 32-bit words, all independent (the law that the seven-word model of H1' gives these three words). The program computes it exactly in rational arithmetic: the filter terms by the subset construction of proof.md 8.3 (the share is checked against CTR_SHARE), the expected nodes of the solver's walk at each of its 33 levels for the 14 outcomes and 4 guesses by the forward and backward pass of Lemma PX, and the good words from the class counts N3_j of Section 17; a passing step adds 56 for the dispatch and 84 for ctr_rest. Nothing is sampled and no message pair is built. Every trial row carries the same observations (the expectations of the events, ex = E[X] as a float, ex_num and ex_den_log2 with E[X] = ex_num / 2^ex_den_log2, share, share_ok, below_premise); the seeds do not enter. Real outer steps of the walk are not run.
experiments.hypothesis: The program outputs E[X] = 11850864922893441 / 2^47 = 84.20545983 under M_X, with share_ok and below_premise true: the exact model mean is below the premise 1369/16 = 85.5625 of H2''. This is an exact computation under the stated model, not a sample and not evidence that the real outer steps follow the model; the transfer to real outer steps is heuristic H2'' (proof.md 10.3). The returned rows hold no message pair, so the checked digest event has no successes by design.
